section_summary: This section moves from a report on the 1934 Soviet–Japanese fishery auction dispute and Japanese fishing industry consolidation to U.S. concerns about Japanese vessels near Alaska. Correspondence considers a treaty to protect Bristol Bay salmon, possible trade concessions, Coast Guard observations, whaling, Aleutian Islands visits, and radio equipment on Japanese fishing vessels. It also contains an Alaska map, file notes, and routing slips.

subfiles.title: Japanese fisheries report, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Reports the Soviet–Japanese fishery auction dispute and developments in Japan’s fishing industry.
subfiles.summary: The report describes Soviet rejection of Japanese bids at the Vladivostok auction over the ruble exchange rate and the resulting diplomatic stalemate. It then discusses proposed fishing company mergers, government oversight, and draft inspection controls for marine exports. A source list closes the report.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese trochus shell fishing
subfiles.about: Points to clippings on Japanese trochus shell fishing near Northern Australia.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Sydney newspaper clippings sent by the U.S. consulate.

subfiles.title: Commerce letter on Japanese fishing in Bristol Bay
subfiles.about: Forwards a Fisheries Bureau memorandum urging consideration of a treaty protecting Alaska salmon.
subfiles.summary: Roper forwards the commissioner’s concerns about Japanese crab vessels and possible salmon packing.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing operations in Bristol Bay, Alaska
subfiles.about: Assesses the threat that Japanese floating canneries could enter Alaska’s salmon fishery.
subfiles.summary: The commissioner reports no authenticated Japanese salmon catch but fears future competition beyond the three-mile limit. He proposes a treaty barring Japanese salmon packing in specified Bering Sea and Bristol Bay waters, while warning that Japan might seek crab trade concessions or revision of the fur-seal treaty.

subfiles.title: Draft-letter background note
subfiles.about: Explains consultations and background materials for draft letters on the Alaska fishery.
subfiles.summary: Records consultations and Commerce’s assent to sharing a letter with the Tariff Commission.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Commerce’s Bristol Bay letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the proposed treaty to protect Bristol Bay salmon.
subfiles.summary: Promises further consideration and an early reply.

subfiles.title: Request for tariff advice on canned crab
subfiles.about: Seeks confidential advice on reducing canned-crab duties as a possible inducement to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull reviews the suspended 1930–31 discussions over protecting Alaskan salmon and asks whether canned-crab duties could be reduced or removed without serious harm to U.S. interests.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Alaska salmon treaty
subfiles.about: Reviews past discussions and possible terms for an agreement with Japan on Alaska salmon.
subfiles.summary: Hull recounts 1930–31 talks in which Japan indicated that lawful high-seas fishing could be restrained only through a treaty offering compensatory privileges. He favors an agreement when practicable and asks the Tariff Commission about crab duties. If concessions prove feasible, he proposes informal talks in Tokyo involving the embassy and a Bureau of Fisheries representative.

subfiles.title: Map of Alaska
subfiles.about: Shows Alaska and surrounding waters relevant to the proposed fishery boundary.
subfiles.summary: A multi-page OCR rendering of an Alaska map, with Cape Avinof among its labels.

subfiles.title: Comment on Navy whaling report
subfiles.about: Notes errors in a Navy report describing Japanese whaling as a new industry.
subfiles.summary: States that Japanese whaling is established and cites a 1932 catch of 1,235 whales.

subfiles.title: Navy report on sale of Norwegian whaling vessels
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese purchase of a Norwegian whaling fleet and speculates on its movements.
subfiles.summary: Lists a factory ship and four whale catchers sold to Japanese interests and raises defense concerns.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Navy whaling report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Navy’s report on Norwegian whaling ships sold to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Puleston for the report.

subfiles.title: Tariff Commission advice on fishery concessions
subfiles.about: Evaluates tariff and port concessions that might support a salmon agreement with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The commission finds limited direct competition between most imported Japanese canned crab and domestic crab. It discusses possible Japanese use of Alaskan ports, likely objections, and alternative duty reductions on dried fish, oysters, and fish specialties; tuna and clams pose greater competitive concerns.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Tariff Commission advice to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards tariff advice and outlines possible next steps toward Japan talks.
subfiles.summary: State sends the tariff opinion and says it would consult the Tokyo embassy before approaching Japan.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Tariff Commission letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges tariff advice and an offer of unpublished fisheries data.
subfiles.summary: Thanks O’Brien for the advice and confidential data offer.

subfiles.title: Commerce response on Alaska salmon negotiations
subfiles.about: Supports informal Tokyo discussions on protecting Alaskan salmon.
subfiles.summary: Commerce agrees that a treaty should be explored before Japan invests in salmon packing. It considers potential tariff concessions less costly than the risk to Alaska’s salmon fishery and awaits the Tokyo embassy’s view.

subfiles.title: Request for Ambassador Grew’s views
subfiles.about: Requests the embassy’s judgment on the timing of a proposed Alaska salmon treaty approach.
subfiles.summary: State sends confidential background documents and asks whether approaching Japan is advisable and timely. It requests a telegraphic affirmative reply and does not authorize negotiations.

subfiles.title: Follow-up telegram to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests views on the salmon treaty and Japanese interest in fur-seal treaty revision.
subfiles.summary: Seeks an early reply and directs the embassy to avoid consulting Japanese officials on either question.

subfiles.title: Treasury forwarding letter on Bering Sea patrol
subfiles.about: Transmits Coast Guard observations of Japanese activity in the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the patrol commander’s 24 October report.

subfiles.title: Japanese activities in Bering Sea, season 1934
subfiles.about: Records Coast Guard sightings of Japanese canneries, trawlers, tenders, and a training vessel.
subfiles.summary: The patrol lists vessel positions, extensive crab net areas, and catches observed during 1934. It reports amicable relations with American cod fishers, a cannery master’s account of vessel movements, and the Hakuyo Maru’s July visit to Dutch Harbor.

subfiles.title: The Whaling Industry of Japan
subfiles.about: Surveys the history, regulation, companies, catches, and products of Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: McClintock traces Japanese whaling from American and Norwegian influence to Toyo Whaling’s dominance. He describes government construction subsidies and licensing, regional stations, species and catch statistics, and the use of whales for oil, food, baleen, and fertilizer. He also notes Toyo’s purchase of Norwegian vessels and questions one company’s product-yield figures.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard forwarding memorandum
subfiles.about: Sends another copy of the Bering Sea patrol report.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the patrol commander’s 24 October report following a telephone conversation.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessels in Bering Sea, season 1934
subfiles.about: Provides Fisheries with Coast Guard observations of Japanese vessels during 1934.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the patrol’s sightings of Japanese crab canneries, tenders, trawlers, and the Hakuyo Maru. It describes net areas, vessel movements, and the training ship’s Dutch Harbor visit.

subfiles.title: Under secretary’s note
subfiles.about: Requests a conversation about the current state of a matter.
subfiles.summary: Asks to discuss the matter and mentions briefing Phillips.

subfiles.title: Phillips memorandum on W. Cameron Forbes’s proposal
subfiles.about: Records Forbes’s call for an agreement limiting Japanese salmon fishing.
subfiles.summary: Forbes claims Japanese vessels threaten U.S. salmon canners and suggests repair facilities and trade concessions as possible inducements. Phillips records the conversation.

subfiles.title: Enclosure routing note
subfiles.about: Notes an enclosure and transmitting correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note refers to transmitting letters of 21 and 28 December.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file note
subfiles.about: Gives a brief instruction concerning an enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Partly illegible handwritten instruction about an enclosure.

subfiles.title: Treasury letter on Japanese lobster fleet proposal
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese proposal to transship lobster catches through Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Says Customs correspondence is enclosed, though a file note records missing enclosures.

subfiles.title: Treasury letter supplying omitted enclosures
subfiles.about: Sends enclosures omitted from the earlier lobster-fleet letter.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the missing Customs correspondence.

subfiles.title: Customs ruling on Japanese fish transshipment
subfiles.about: Addresses whether Japanese vessels may transship catches at Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Finds no Customs objection if immediate-export procedures are followed; refers navigation-law questions elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Los Angeles collector’s report on Japanese lobster interests
subfiles.about: Reports an inquiry about Japanese fishing in Mexican waters and transshipment at Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: A lawyer describes Japanese lobster concessions off Lower California. Cohn sees no apparent legal bar but urges close Navy and State scrutiny.

subfiles.title: Note on American and Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Summarizes vessel numbers and fishing activity around Alaska.
subfiles.summary: OCR is damaged; the note compares American fishing activity with reported Japanese canneries and tenders.

subfiles.title: Aleutian Islands: Japanese espionage activities therein
subfiles.about: Assesses alleged Japanese espionage and a proposal to close the Aleutians to foreign vessels.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum finds no evidence that reported espionage is particularly serious. It warns that closing the islands could provoke Japan, complicate fur-seal treaty cooperation, and damage prospects for an Alaska salmon agreement. It describes existing procedures for Japanese public-vessel visits.

subfiles.title: Note on Japanese fishing-vessel radios
subfiles.about: Refers Navy concerns about Japanese vessel radios to an interdepartmental committee.
subfiles.summary: Chipman agrees to consider radio provisions in a fisheries-vessel bill.

subfiles.title: Navy letter on Japanese fishing-vessel radios
subfiles.about: Raises defense concerns about radio-equipped Japanese fishing vessels near U.S. coasts.
subfiles.summary: The Navy alleges that some vessels observe fleet exercises and contact Japanese ships at sea; it forwards two enclosures.
